scope: Theorem 2.3 (Grassmann expansion consequence) of the manuscript “Perfect completeness for 2-to-1 games” (preprints/Perfect-completeness-for-2-to-1-games-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 105 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 2691ba6bd2ac7159), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 7. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For each 0 < ζ < 1, there are α > 0, an integer r ≥ 1, and ℓ0 such that, for every ℓ ≥ ℓ0 and then every sufficiently large N, the following holds. Every nonempty set of vertices with retention at least ζ has density at least α in an interval {L : A0 ⊆ L ⊆ B0, dim L = ℓ}, dim A0 + codim B0 ≤ r. The constants α, r, ℓ0 depend only on ζ; the threshold for N may also depend on ℓ.
